checks.finding: Architecture and Ownership defines Host Adapter, Shared SDD Core, Capability Resolver/Registry, target artifacts, provider adapter, normalized evidence, and ownership boundaries with a concrete flow.
The ownership flow is directional from host through core, resolver, artifacts, optional provider, and normalized evidence back to core; no reverse dependency or cycle is specified.

The Resolution Model and verification-plan fields define required, conditional, not-applicable-with-reason, and not-run/unknown evidence states; provider evidence includes target, binding, and simulated/real provenance. No new persisted data model is introduced.

Consumer Disposition identifies the existing resolver, Registry, host adapters, DesignSync boundary, CI boundary, and contract-check surfaces, with additive selection behavior and explicit deferred provider operations.

Security boundaries are covered by no provider writes in scope, separation of provider bindings from core capability data, explicit consent/no-egress behavior, fail-closed required-check handling, and mock-versus-real evidence labeling.
This staged architecture-boundary migration has no frontend or backend service implementation; UX/provider applicability and existing CI/MCP boundaries are documented separately.

Test and Evidence Strategy covers consumer inventory, five target examples, legacy/hybrid compatibility, UI-provider consent and fallback states, provider-boundary evidence, host matrix semantics, and exclusion of artifact/promotion claims.

Every component in the architecture and Consumer Disposition is named with an owner and disposition; deferred provider, promotion, and facet-native work is explicitly bounded rather than left implicit.
The design cites ADR-0016, ADR-0017, and ADR-0018 for workflow axes, gate-stage ownership, and provider-binding separation; each cited path is an existing canonical ADR.
No UI surface is implemented; UX and frontend layer documents explicitly declare the non-rendered scope, while the optional UI provider preserves existing design-system and consent semantics.
The design keeps domain-neutral capability identities separate from provider bindings, preserves legacy and facet-hybrid compatibility, and does not invent a second gate source of truth.
